beats.text: As organizations adopt AI across more applications, a pattern is emerging. The AI requirements are remarkably similar, whatever the application.
Case management, analytics, a knowledge portal, a CRM, a legacy application. Each one needs the same five things.
So each team builds them again. The real cost isn't the duplicated effort. It's that AI becomes an application by application project, rather than something the organization has.
Another approach is to provide those capabilities once, as a shared service that applications simply connect to.
What stays with each application is the part that genuinely differs. What questions matter, what data matters, and what each kind of user needs.
The intent isn't to standardize every application. It's to standardize the AI capabilities that nearly every application requires.
As AI adoption accelerates, the important architectural question may not be which model to use, but where AI belongs within the enterprise architecture.
